title: Find an antiderivative
text: Integrate by parts twice. An antiderivative is $$\frac{1}{2} e^{\left(-x\right)} \left(sin\left(x\right)-cos\left(x\right)\right)$$.

title: Take the limit
text: As $$x$$ goes to $$\infty$$, the antiderivative goes to $$0$$. At $$x=0$$ it equals $$\frac{-1}{2}$$, so the integral is $$0-\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$$.
